title: Marcos calls for renewed political will, cooperation to achieve SDGs
summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday called for a renewed political will, stronger partnerships, and evidence-based cooperation to realize the United Nations Sustainable Development…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday called for a renewed political will, stronger partnerships, and evidence-based cooperation to realize the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) by 2030.
During the 16th ASEAN-UN Summit, Marcos pointed out that only 36% of the accessible SDG targets “are on track” less than four years away from the 2030 deadline.

“Achieving these goals requires renewed political will, stronger partnerships with the private sector, and cooperation that is evidence-based and responsive to the needs of its members, especially developing countries,” the President said.

Marcos said that through the ASEAN-UN Complementarities Initiative, ASEAN is hoped to substantially contribute to advancing progress in these goals by aligning ASEAN 2045 with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
He likewise welcomed the UN General Assembly’s adoption of the resolution commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia.
Marcos said that the adoption served as a “reaffirmation of conduct for interstate relations in our region and beyond.”
He also noted the first year of the ASEAN-UN Plan of Action 2026-2030.
“Our cooperation spans peace and security---from combating trafficking in persons, online scams, and illicit drugs, to peacekeeping and keeping Southeast Asia free of nuclear weapons,” Marcos said.

“It extends to trade facilitation, digital transformation, the blue economy, the ASEAN Power Grid, and sustainable minerals development. It also covers health, food, security, disaster management, climate action, and the protection of women, children, persons with disabilities, and science and technology cooperation,” he added.

Secretary-General António Guterres, on the other hand, congratulated the Philippines for what he described as a “successful conduct” of the first parliamentary polls in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
He said the elections fully consolidated a “remarkable peace process” in the region.
“This should serve as an example well beyond the Philippines and this region,” Guterres said.
The UN chief, however, lamented the impacts of the tensions between Russia and Ukraine, as well as those in the Middle East, Strait of Hormuz, and the Red Sea, on ASEAN.
“I want to reaffirm the unconditional commitment of the United Nations to defend the rights and freedoms of navigation in all situations,” Guterres said.
He also expressed concern over the continuing crisis in Myanmar.

“Human suffering has reached epic proportions. I call on all parties to protect civilians, uphold international law, and allow safe, sustained, and unhindered humanitarian access,” he said. —AOL, GMA News
